10.q: An omni-bearing selector (OBS) shows full deflection to the left when within range of a serviceable VOR. What angular deviation are you from the selected radial?

o: The receiver adds 30Hz to the variable signal before combining it with the reference signal
The transmitter changes the frequency of the variable signal by 30Hz either side of the allocated frequency each time it rotates

16.q: If the reference phase differs by 30° from the variable phase, the radial from the VOR station will be:

o: at the half-way point between the aircraft and the station

3.q: An aircraft at FL400; the VOR is at MSL. Maximum reception range?

ex.10: Full-scale deflection on a VOR CDI is 10° (5 dots × 2°).
ex.13: The aircraft is due south (180° T). Radials use the variation at the VOR: 180 − 13 E = 167.
ex.18: Due south of the VOR: 180° T + 10° W (VOR variation) = 190.
ex.19: The aircraft is west of the VOR: 270° T − 15° E (VOR variation) = 255.
ex.23: Half-width 5 NM ÷ tan 5.5° ≈ 52 NM from each VOR: about 105 NM apart.
ex.26: Bearing 090° from the VOR means the aircraft is on the 090 radial; to go TO the station select 270.
ex.28: 5 NM at 100 NM = 3°; at 2° per dot that is 1.5 dots.
ex.35: 30 000 ft ≈ 5 NM; at 45° the radius equals the height: 5 NM.
